result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a concrete single-source plan with version-tagged differences. B wins mainly because it assigns chapter ownership to the two writers, which A never does, and it says to fix and log drift while diffing before retiring and redirecting the old copies. A gives stronger tooling detail and a staged rollout by priority, but it fills the plan with invented effort figures and builds out more CI and tooling than two writers need. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B gives the more concrete single-source mechanics, with drift buckets, conditionals, separate per-version files for big differences, and a cutover diff, but it never says which of the two writers owns what. A splits ownership between Writer 1 and Writer 2 and adds a fix-checked-across-versions rule, though it drifts into extras like an engineering definition of done and monthly reviews. Both make up time figures and lean toward a full migration rather than starting with the most-fixed pages.
